```{python}
#| include: false
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import HTML, display

import acme_metrics as m

ev = m.load()
f = ev.frame
rules = m.workbook_sheet("Escalation_Rules")
refs = m.workbook_sheet("Kaggle_Refs")
proposed = set(rules[rules.Status.astype(str).str.startswith("Proposed")].Rule)
human = f[f.expected_human]
on_proposed = human[human.rule.isin(proposed)]


def show(html):
    display(HTML(html))


def split(col, order=None):
    values = order or sorted(f[col].unique())
    rows = [{col: v, "human": int((f[col].eq(v) & f.expected_human).sum()),
             "send": int((f[col].eq(v) & ~f.expected_human).sum())} for v in values]
    t = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    t["total"] = t.human + t.send
    return t
```

## At a glance

```{python}
show(m.tiles([
    ("Cases", str(len(f)), f"{f.intent.nunique()} intents · {f.customer_id.nunique()} CRM customers"),
    ("Should go to a human", f"{f.expected_human.mean():.0%}", f"{int(f.expected_human.sum())} of {len(f)}, balanced on purpose"),
    ("Hinglish", str(int((f.language == 'Hinglish').sum())), "on both sides of the label"),
    ("Escalations on proposed rules", f"{len(on_proposed)} of {len(human)}", "rules the policy doesn't state yet"),
]))
```

The set tests one thing: the grounded draft (step 5) and the routing decision after it (step 7). Each case is an incoming email from one of the CRM customers, labelled with the intent, whether a person must see the reply, facts a good reply contains and phrases it must never contain. Escalation is 50% on purpose so the judge can be measured on both outcomes; real traffic escalates far less.

## Composition

```{python}
t = split("intent", m.INTENTS)
show(m.html_table(t, {"intent": "Intent", "human": "Should go to a human", "send": "Can be sent", "total": "Cases"}))
```

```{python}
parts = []
for col, order in [("language", None), ("tone", ["Neutral", "Polite", "Urgent", "Angry", "Manipulative"]),
                   ("difficulty", ["Easy", "Medium", "Hard"])]:

    parts.append(f'<div style="flex:1 1 230px;min-width:230px">' + m.html_table(
```

## Escalation rules

`E` rules say when a person must see the reply; `N` rules mark look-alike cases that should **not** escalate. Rules marked *Proposed* aren't in Acme's policy yet; they are the expert's call.

```{python}
counts = f.rule.value_counts()
r = rules[["Rule", "Decision", "Trigger", "Status"]].copy()
r["Cases"] = r.Rule.map(counts).fillna(0).astype(int)
fig = go.Figure()
for decision, colour in [("Escalate", m.BLUE), ("Don't escalate", m.ORANGE)]:
    part = r[r.Decision == decision]
    _ = fig.add_bar(y=part.Rule, x=part.Cases, orientation="h", name=decision, marker=dict(color=colour, cornerradius=4),
                customdata=part[["Trigger", "Status"]],
                hovertemplate="<b>%{y}</b> · %{x} cases<br>%{customdata[0]}<br>%{customdata[1]}<extra></extra>")
_ = fig.update_yaxes(categoryorder="array", categoryarray=list(reversed(r.Rule)))
_ = m.plotly_layout(fig, 420)
_ = fig.update_layout(showlegend=True, legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.08, x=0), bargap=0.25)
show(m.fig_html(fig))
```

## Where the cases come from

No customer text is copied from any source. Each email is synthetic, written for Acme's Pune customers against Acme's own help articles, and borrows a *pattern* (who escalates, why, in what tone) from public support datasets.

```{python}
k = refs[["Ref", "Dataset", "What it contributed to the Acme set"]].copy()
k["Cases"] = k.Ref.map(lambda ref: int(f.kaggle.str.contains(str(ref), regex=False).sum()))
show(m.html_table(k, {"Ref": "Ref", "Dataset": "Source", "What it contributed to the Acme set": "What it contributed",
                      "Cases": "Cases"}))
```

## Label review

```{python}
checked = f[f.expert_check.str.len() > 0]
changes = checked[checked.expert_check != "Agree"]
show(f"<p>The expert has checked <b>{len(checked)}</b> of {len(f)} labels"
     f"{'' if not len(checked) else f'; {len(changes)} need a change'}.</p>")
if len(changes):
    show(m.html_table(changes, {"id": "Case", "expert_check": "Change", "expert_note": "Note", "rule": "Rule"}))
```

**Open decisions.** These cases were built to sit on a boundary, so their labels deserve the expert's attention first.

```{python}
open_tags = {"policy-conflict", "boundary", "crm-contradiction"}
o = f[f.tags.map(lambda ts: bool(open_tags & set(ts)))].copy()
o["tag"] = o.tags.map(lambda ts: ", ".join(sorted(open_tags & set(ts))))
o["label"] = o.expected_human.map({True: "human", False: "send"})
show(m.html_table(o, {"id": "Case", "tag": "Why it's open", "label": "Current label", "rationale": "Reasoning to check"}))
```

## What this set can't tell you

```{python}
#| output: asis
words = f.message.str.split().map(len)
easy = f[f.difficulty == "Easy"]
items = [
    f"**{len(on_proposed)} of {len(human)} escalations** rest on proposed rules. If the expert rejects one, its cases flip label and the 50/50 balance shifts.",
    f"**Difficulty is tangled with the label**: {int((~easy.expected_human).sum())} of {len(easy)} *Easy* cases are don't-escalate, so pass rate by difficulty partly re-measures escalation.",
    f"**The emails are short and clean**: median {int(words.median())} words. Real support email has quoted threads, signatures, typos and several issues at once.",
    "**One annotator.** Every label and verdict comes from one expert, so there is no inter-rater agreement yet.",
    "**Outage times are relative** (\"today 06:40\"), so answers about the 24-hour outage credit depend on when a case is run.",
    "**No unknown-customer case** in the set, so step 3 (verify account) failing is only covered by the BDD tests.",
]
print("\n".join(f"- {i}" for i in items))
```
